eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from the National Weather Service and private forecasters points to a moderating marine layer and weak onshore flow arriving ahead of May 29, keeping Seattle’s daytime maximum in the mid- to upper-50s or low-60s. This pattern, driven by a building surface high offshore, limits afternoon heating through persistent low stratus and light southerly winds that advect cooler Pacific air inland. Ensemble spreads remain modest, with slight differences in cloud cover timing and boundary-layer mixing creating the tight clustering between 56–61 °F outcomes. Historical late-May climatology favors highs near 65 °F, but the current synoptic setup has already produced cooler-than-normal readings earlier in the week, anchoring trader expectations around the lower end of the seasonal range while leaving room for modest warming if the marine layer erodes earlier than anticipated.
